subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should the remaining work add Mission Control workspace-wide editing and/or host-system browsing, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: Current main intentionally split read-only workspace browsing from mutations, while this request crosses into arbitrary workspace edits and host filesystem access that can expose secrets or destructive operations.

options.title: Approve workspace-only design first
options.body: Continue with a bounded workspace-scoped API/UI design for read and admin-gated mutations, using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/62417 as the review path while deferring host-system browsing.

options.title: Keep read-only plus bootstrap editing
options.body: Treat the current read-only workspace browser and allowlisted `agents.files.*` editor as the accepted boundary until stronger user demand or proof justifies more file mutation surface.

options.title: Open a separate system-scope design
options.body: If host filesystem browsing is desired, require a separate security-reviewed design with explicit opt-in, authorization, auditing, read/write limits, and recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only design first
recommendation.body: Continue with a bounded workspace-scoped API/UI design for read and admin-gated mutations, using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/62417 as the review path while deferring host-system browsing.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the landed read-only workspace API/viewer slices and are the strongest current owner for the remaining product/security boundary.
